name: iHeartMedia, Inc.
addedReason: down ~29% premarket after a weaker Q3 2026 report

marketCap.note: Predates the Nov 9 earnings/guidance cut and subsequent price decline; current market cap would be materially lower

debt.note: Company-reported net debt figure elsewhere is ~$4.7B — not the same metric; both retained for reference

pe.note: Q3 2026 loss of $0.06/share vs a consensus of breakeven; trailing P/E not meaningful

growth.note: Ex-political revenue growth was ~0.9%; missed ~$1.05B consensus. Podcast revenue +24% to $174M; Digital Audio Group +14% to $389M; Multiplatform (broadcast radio) -5% to $562M with segment adjusted EBITDA -43%

price.note: Per Kalkine; two other sources describe the same post-earnings move with very different magnitudes (-36.9% per StockStory; ~-15% 'after the close' per Quiver Quant) — see conflicts. A pre-earnings quote of $1.87 (market cap $317.32M) was dated 2026-11-06.

catalysts.headline: Law firm 'SueWallSt' issued a shareholder-investigation notice regarding potential securities claims tied to the stock's collapse (solicitation-style release, not a regulatory action)
iHeartMedia fell ~29% premarket after its Q3 2026 report; no further detail (reported figures, consensus comparison) located beyond the aggregator mover headline this session.
IHRT shares fell sharply following the Q3 report and guidance cut; magnitude varies by source (see conflicts)
iHeartMedia CEO warned major advertisers are delaying spending as economic uncertainty bites, cited as driver of continued share weakness the day after earnings

iHeartMedia reported Q3 2026 results: revenue ~$1.03B (+3.3% YoY, missing ~$1.05B consensus); adjusted EBITDA of $170M (below guided $180-220M range); GAAP loss of $0.06/share vs breakeven consensus; cut FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $550-600M (from ~$800M) and FCF guidance to ~$50M (from ~$200M); took a $209M impairment on station license valuations
catalysts.impact: Major guidance cut cited to weak broadcast-radio ad demand and faster shift to programmatic buying; shares fell sharply

catalysts.headline: iHeartMedia Q3 2026 results: revenue $1.03B (+3.3% YoY, +1% ex-political); Adjusted EBITDA $170.5M, down 16.7% YoY and below the company's own $180-220M plan; GAAP EPS loss of $0.06 (vs -$0.02 est.); Multiplatform Group (broadcast) segment adjusted EBITDA fell 42.9%; Digital Audio Group revenue +13.8% but segment EBITDA -2.3%; podcast revenue +24.4% to $173.7M; free cash flow -$10.4M for the quarter; cash fell to $139.7M from $174.4M at June 2026; company cut full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $550M-$600M from the prior ~$800M target cited on prior calls, largely on weaker-than-expected political advertising, advertiser spending delays amid macro uncertainty, and a shift to programmatic audio buying
catalysts.impact: Shares fell sharply; reported after-hours decline of approximately 35-37%, with the stock later touching a new 52-week low intraday around -66% to $0.598-$0.6095 before settling near $0.62

catalysts.headline: iHeartMedia entered a Transaction Support Agreement with holders representing 80% of existing debt to extend debt maturities by three years and strengthen its balance sheet

conflicts: Post-earnings share-price move magnitude: Kalkine reports -61.58% to $0.68 close on 2026-11-10; StockStory reports -36.9%; Quiver Quant reports shares fell ~15% 'after the close' on Nov 9 — all three describe the same underlying event (Q3 2026 earnings/guidance cut) but give materially different percentages.
Q3 2026 revenue: $1.03B (company release, via Morningstar/Benzinga) vs $997M (Quiver Quant).
Shares outstanding: 154.79M (Fox Business/Equibles) vs 150,640,000 (MarketBeat) vs 129,552,146 (a separate Equibles short-interest page).
Debt: gross total debt of ~$5,024.3M (Kalkine) is a different measure than the company-cited net debt of ~$4.7B; not to be conflated.
pendingFilings: 8-K ~2026-11-09 (Q3 2026 results, not independently confirmed in EDGAR search)
notes: Extremely volatile week: debt-restructuring news (Nov 7), Q3 earnings and a major guidance cut (Nov 9), and a sharp but inconsistently-reported price decline (Nov 10). Recommend confirming the exact post-earnings closing price from a live/primary quote source before publishing a specific changePct for 2026-11-13.
